summary: @servicetitan/form preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: The package's `preinstall` hook runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads the Bun runtime zip from `github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip`, extracts the `bun` binary to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against `math_init.js` — a 727KB sibling file that is heavily obfuscated with a rotating string-array (`WV8StW`), a large numeric char-code lookup table (`n7gIxM`), and a custom-alphabet base64-like decoder (`hc1jfK9`). The payload carries a `// @bun @bun-cjs` header and is not human-readable; its behavior is unrelated to the package's advertised UI form functionality. The setup script itself is `_0x`-style obfuscated and performs no hash or signature verification on the fetched runtime. This is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern: an obfuscated payload is executed at install time via a freshly-downloaded second runtime, evading Node-based scanning and consuming the installer's machine as an execution target for opaque, attacker-controlled code on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
